0.original: Gulool Ja wishes to go and collect his flower for the funeral.

24.original: Speak with Gossan at Praxis Park.

48.original: Papa always said he didn't want a somber funeral, so we celebrated his life together with our victory. I'm sure he would've loved it...

49.original: I like to think he was watching us from the world beyond, filling his cup every time we filled our own.

50.original: Although I've been in the Backroom before, there was no time to see the sights. I should like to take a closer look at the equipment.

51.original: It's a relief to see that Gulool Ja is doing well. He's been through too much for one so young.

52.original: From a group that plotted to undermine a tyrant king from the shadows to one that aids their fellow citizens in the open... Oblivion has come a long way.

53.original: For the people to take it on themselves to organize and hold the funeral... It speaks to their enduring love for Sphene.

57.original: The flowers are being handed out at Praxis Park. I'm thinking of heading over there now.

58.original: We'll join you. There's a man I would like to speak with─Gossan. He was apparently Sphene's aide, and the one who sent us the invitation.

60.original: All correspondence was being handled by the Wing of Reflection, so this is my first time speaking with Gossan.

62.original: Wuk Lamat's attendance will surely help strengthen relations between the two nations. I get the strong impression that both Tuliyollal and Alexandria wish to put this tragic past behind them.

63.original: Judging from all the activity, I presume the funeral will be held here.

64.original: While it appears souls are still being issued, supply must be limited now that they're no longer being harvested. The grim faces in the queue tell the tale.

65.original: It makes sense that Sphene had loyal aides such as Gossan, given how much time she dedicated to walking among her people.

67.original: I'm Vow Wuk Lamat of Tuliyollal. Thank you for extending us an invitation to Queen Sphene's funeral.

68.original: We are honored, truly. I had seen you before from a distance, but never had the pleasure.

69.original: I am Gossan, former chief aide to the queen. Since her passing, I have been responsible for administering affairs of state.

70.original: Um, can we get our flowers here?

71.original: Yes, Your Majesty. The flowers are being handed out at the counter yonder, alongside the regulators.

72.original: What? We need to wear regulators for the funeral?

73.original: Ah, rest assured they are not a requirement. We're aware your people do not use them.

74.original: You see, people in the Alexandria of old wore tokens of mourning upon their persons when attending funerals.

75.original: As such tokens were black, it was suggested that we might wear regulators painted the same color.

76.original: We've yet to produce enough for everyone, but we're distributing them as we are able.

78.original: Yet regulator or no, the important thing is that we remember Queen Sphene. Remember her and her kindness as you make an offering of your flower.

80.original: The proceedings will soon begin in this plaza. Please take your place once you have your flower.

81.original: I'm sorry. I shouldn't have brought that up...

82.original: I hope the altar can provide comfort to those who need it.

83.original: Seeing that child reminded me of myself. Of how hard it was for me to accept that Grandfather was gone.

84.original: But that sadness is what gave me the strength to come this far, and I would never choose to forget it. Never.

85.original: This seems a good place to continue our conversation.

86.original: Simply leaving Alexandria won't solve all their problems, I fear. The problem runs deeper than that.

87.original: Hey, Gulool Ja? Do you really know nothing at all about your mother?

88.original: Shale searched the system for information on residents, but the only Mamool Ja she found listed were my father and me.

89.original: Even if she died and was erased from people's memories, she should've been there. But she wasn't...

90.original: Well, that you're here means she was here too, inside the dome. There can't be any other way about it.

92.original: Perhaps we should try looking again.

93.original: Do you want to know your mother?

94.original: Maybe... It's hard to explain. I'm not sad, but I feel like...like I'm missing something.

95.original: So even if it makes me feel sad, I want to know my mother.

96.original: I think so. Even if it makes me feel sad, I want to know her.

97.original: So I want to try looking again. And if I don't find anything this time, I'll give up.

98.original: I see... Well, if that's what you want...

100.original: I'd like to help as well, and I believe I speak for the others too.

101.original: But...I can't bother you with this. You already came for the funeral...

102.original: We came here not only for the funeral, but to see whether all was well in Alexandria. We're not about to leave just yet.

105.original: Besides, in seeking to learn about your mother, we're bound to learn about your father as well.

106.original: By retracing the steps of this man who kept his own counsel, we may gain knowledge that can serve the people of Alexandria.
